title: Deep learning on ECGs predicts left atrial function and later cardiovascular events
summary: A deep-learning model trained on 12-lead ECGs paired with 21,749 UK Biobank cardiac magnetic resonance scans predicts left atrial structure and function. In two external cohorts the model-derived measures were associated with new-onset atrial fibrillation, heart failure and ischemic stroke after adjustment, and cardioembolic stroke risk rose 66% per standard deviation of left atrial volume.
ai_technology: Deep-learning model mapping 12-lead ECGs to cardiac magnetic resonance measures of the left atrium

evidence.tested: Two external cohorts for associations with incident AF, heart failure and stroke; exploratory comparison with a clinical risk tool and NT-proBNP.
evidence.unknown: Observational associations; no evidence that using the model improves outcomes; abstract only; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning inferred imaging-derived atrial measures from ECGs.
